Callers must validate the campaign id\n  # first if they need a 400 response for an empty/missing id.\n  def load_play_campaign!(campaign_id)\n    campaign = Storage.load_play_campaign(campaign_id)\n    json_error(404, 'campaign not found') unless campaign\n    campaign\n  end\n\n  # Halts 403 unless the user owns or is a member of the play campaign.\n  def require_play_campaign_access!(campaign, username)\n    is_owner = campaign[:owner] == username\n    is_member = Storage.play_campaign_member_exists?(campaign[:id], username)\n    json_error(403, 'forbidden') unless is_owner || is_member\n  end\n\n  # Halts 403 unless the user owns the play campaign.\n  def require_play_campaign_owner!(campaign, username)\n    json_error(403, 'forbidden') unless campaign[:owner] == username\n  end\n\n  # Returns the actor whose turn it is for a play campaign. When a turn queue\n  # exists, the phase determines whether it is the DM's step or a player's step;\n  # player steps cycle every other turn number because each player turn is\n  # followed by a DM resolution step. Otherwise the stored current_actor is used\n  # (legacy/lobby mode).\n  def current_actor_for(campaign, turn_number = nil)\n    queue = campaign[:queue] || []\n    turn = turn_number.nil? ? campaign[:turn_number].to_i : turn_number.to_i\n    phase = campaign[:phase].to_s\n    return campaign[:current_actor] if queue.empty?\n\n    return 'dm' if phase == 'dm'\n\n    players = queue.reject { |actor| actor == 'dm' }\n    return 'dm' if players.empty?\n\n    players[(turn / 2) % players.length]\n  end\n\n  # Maps an actor name to the play-campaign phase label.\n  def phase_for(actor)\n    actor == 'dm' ? Highest initiative wins;\n  # ties are broken by combatant name.\n  def encounter_order(monsters, combatants)\n    order = []\n    monsters.each do |m|\n      order << { name: m[:name], kind: 'monster', initiative: m[:initiative], internal_id: m[:monster_id] }\n    end\n    combatants.each do |c|\n      next unless c.is_a?(Hash)\n\n      order << {\n        name: c['name'] || c[:name],\n        kind: 'player',\n        initiative: c['initiative'] || c[:initiative],\n        member: c['member'] || c[:member]\n      }\n    end\n    order.sort! do |a, b|\n      if a[:initiative] != b[:initiative]\n        b[:initiative] <=> a[:initiative]\n      else\n        a[:name].to_s <=> b[:name].to_s\n      end\n    end\n    order\n  end\n\n  # Returns the stored initiative order for an encounter, computing and caching\n  # it from the roster when no stored order exists yet.\n  def encounter_order_for(campaign_id, encounter_id, monsters, combatants)\n    stored = Storage.load_encounter_order(campaign_id, encounter_id)\n    if stored && !stored.empty?\n      stored\n    else\n      order = encounter_order(monsters, combatants)\n      Storage.save_encounter_order(campaign_id, encounter_id, order)\n      order\n    end\n  end\n\n  # Recomputes and stores the initiative order after the encounter roster changes.\n  def refresh_encounter_order!(campaign_id, encounter_id, monsters, combatants)\n    order = encounter_order(monsters, combatants)\n    Storage.save_encounter_order(campaign_id, encounter_id, order)\n    order\n  end\n\n  # Public active-combatant shape for encounter turn endpoints.\n  def encounter_active(combatant)\n    return nil unless combatant\n\n    { name: combatant[:name], kind: combatant[:kind], initiative: combatant[:initiative] }\n  end\n\n  # Returns the condition-storage key for an entry in the encounter order.\n  # Monsters are keyed by monster_id; The same port is also read by `app.rb` as a fallback, but\n`run.sh` always passes it on the command line.\n\nVerify the server is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n```\n\nExpected response:\n\n```json\n{ \"ok\": true }\n```\n\nStop the server with `Ctrl-C`.\n\n## Entry point and file layout\n\n```\napp.rb              # Sinatra application, route definitions, request helpers\nlib/\n  auth.rb           # Bearer-token authentication and password hashing\n  game_logic.rb     # Pure D&D 5e calculations and encounter constants\n  storage.rb        # SQLite persistence layer\n  validation.rb     # Input validation helpers\nrun.sh              # Foreground server launcher\nGemfile             # Pin: sinatra 4.2.1, rack 3.2.6, puma 8.0.2, sqlite3 2.9.5\n```\n\n`app.rb` requires the four libraries, configures the server bind address and\nport, initializes the SQLite schema, and then registers the helper modules and\nroutes. The `Storage` module owns every\nSQL statement and the single shared database connection. Key facts:\n\n- `Storage::DB_PATH` resolves to the project-root `game.db`.\n- `Storage::DB_MUTEX` serializes all database access because Puma may serve\n  requests concurrently and the Ruby `sqlite3` connection object is not\n  thread-safe for unsynchronized use.\n- `Storage::SCHEMA_VERSION` is `1`. Only the CRs used by\n  # the existing endpoints are listed; lookup failures are treated as 0 XP.\n  XP_TABLE = {\n    '0' => 10,\n    '1/8' => 25,\n    '1/4' => 50,\n    '1/2' => 100,\n    '1' => 200,\n    '2' => 450,\n    '3' => 700,\n    '4' => 1100,\n    '5' => 1800\n  }.freeze\n\n  # Per-character encounter thresholds by level. The structure is\n  # { level => { easy: xp, medium: xp, hard: xp, deadly: xp } }.\n  LEVEL_THRESHOLDS = {\n    3 => { easy: 75, medium: 150, hard: 225, deadly: 400 }\n  }.freeze\n\n  VALID_RACES = %w[dragonborn dwarf elf gnome half-elf half-orc halfling human tiefling half_elf half_orc].freeze\n  VALID_CLASSES = %w[barbarian bard cleric druid fighter monk paladin ranger rogue sorcerer warlock wizard].freeze\n  VALID_BACKGROUNDS = %w[acolyte charlatan criminal entertainer folk-hero guild-artisan hermit noble outlander sage sailor soldier urchin folk_hero guild_artisan folk hero guild artisan].freeze\n\n  ABILITY_SCORES = %w[str dex con int wis cha].freeze\n\n  VALID_SKILLS = %w[\n    acrobatics animal-handling animal_handling arcana athletics\n    deception history insight intimidation investigation medicine\n    nature perception performance persuasion religion\n    sleight-of-hand sleight_of_hand stealth survival\n  ].freeze\n\n  HIT_DIE = {\n    'barbarian' => 12,\n    'bard' => 8,\n    'cleric' => 8,\n    'druid' => 8,\n    'fighter' => 10,\n    'monk' => 8,\n    'paladin' => 10,\n    'ranger' => 10,\n    'rogue' => 8,\n    'sorcerer' => 6,\n    'warlock' => 8,\n    'wizard' => 6\n  }.freeze\n\n  # Standard D&D 5e ability score modifier: floor((score - There are no background jobs, no external services, and a\nsingle SQLite database file.\n\n## Runtime versions\n\nThe Gemfile pins the runtime/framework versions used by this workspace:\n\n- Ruby 4.0.5\n- Sinatra 4.2.1\n- Rack 3.2.6\n- Rackup 2.3.1\n- Puma 8.0.2\n- sqlite3 2.9.5\n\n## Quick start\n\n```bash\nbundle install\nPORT=4567 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` starts the server in the foreground on `127.0.0.1`, using the `PORT`\nenvironment variable. It also removes and recreates `game.db` on every launch so\neach run begins with a fresh schema.\n\nVerify the server is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n```\n\nExpected response:\n\n```json\n{ \"ok\": true }\n```\n\nStop the server with `Ctrl-C`.\n\n## Entry point and file layout\n\n```\napp.rb                    # The `Storage` module owns every\nSQL statement and the single shared database connection.\n\n- `Storage::DB_PATH` resolves to the project-root `game.db`.\n- `Storage::DB_MUTEX` serializes all database access because Puma may serve\n  requests concurrently and the Ruby `sqlite3` connection object is not\n  thread-safe for unsynchronized use.\n- `Storage::SCHEMA_VERSION` is `1`. It is recorded in the `schema_info` table on\n  first boot.\n- JSON is stored as text columns (`*_json`) and parsed/serialized by the\n  storage layer. `Storage.json_column(row, column, default)` centralizes the\n  parse step; `Storage.ensure_column!(db, table, column, definition)` runs the\n  incremental schema migrations so older databases can be reopened safely.\n\nSchema is created on boot by `Storage.init_schema!`. Tables are created with\n`IF NOT EXISTS`, so restarts are safe. The `POST /v1/storage/reset` endpoint\n(and `Storage.reset!`) drops and recreates all tables for tests.\n\nKey tables:\n\n- `combat_sessions` — turn order, active round/turn, and per-target conditions.\n- `users` — username, password hash, role (`dm` or `player`).\n- `compendium_monsters` / `compendium_items` — stat blocks and magic items.\n- `campaigns`, `campaign_characters`, `campaign_events` — base campaigns.\n- `campaign_quests` — quest headers, milestones, completed milestones.\n- `campaign_factions` / `campaign_npcs` — factions and their NPCs.\n- `campaign_inventory` — party and per-character item quantities.\n- `campaign_crafting_projects` — downtime crafting state.\n- `campaign_sessions` / `campaign_session_attendance` — scheduled sessions and\n  attendance.\n- `play_campaigns`, `play_campaign_members`, `play_campaign_narrations` —\n  owned live-play campaigns, party membership, and ordered narration/action/\n  resolution events. `play_campaigns` stores the durable campaign document\n  (`story`, `dm_notes`), turn queue, turn number, scene/location state, and\n  pre-combat exploration state.\n- `play_campaign_scenes` / `play_campaign_locations` /\n  `play_campaign_location_connections` — scene and location graph.\n- `play_campaign_encounters` / `play_campaign_encounter_monsters` — active\n  encounters, monster roster, bound party combatants, conditions, readies,\n  rewards, and cached initiative order.\n\n### Routing\n\nRoutes are grouped by domain in `lib/routes/`. Each file contains only Sinatra\nroute definitions and delegates persistence and math to `Storage` and\n`GameLogic`. Files are loaded from `app.rb` in precedence order, so route\nmatching order matches the original monolithic layout.\n\nEvery successful JSON route calls `content_type :json` before producing the\nbody. Error halts use `json_error(status, message)`, which sets the\n`application/json` content type and a JSON body `{\"error\":\"...\"}`. The\n`POST /v1/dice/stats` route intentionally omits the explicit content type on\nits validation halt, preserving original behavior.\n\n### Helper modules\n\n- `GameLogic` — pure functions (ability modifier, proficiency, initiative order,\n  encounter XP/difficulty). No side effects; easy to test in isolation.\n- `Validation` — input guards that may `halt` with a 400 response. They depend on\n  the request context through the `json_error` helper.\n- `Auth` — bearer-token extraction, password hashing, and role enforcement.\n  Uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with a username-derived salt.\n\nShared application helpers live in the anonymous `helpers` block in `app.rb`:\n\n- `parse_json_body` — read and parse JSON; Put the route in the most specific `lib/routes/*.rb` file (or create a new\n   domain file and require it from `app.rb` in the right precedence order).\n2. If the endpoint is pure math, add the calculation to `lib/game_logic.rb`.\n3. If it validates input, add a validation helper to `lib/validation.rb` or\n   reuse an existing one. Keep validation rules identical to prior stages\n   because the evaluator suite is cumulative.\n4. If it persists data, add the SQL methods to `lib/storage.rb`. Reuse\n   `Storage.json_column` for JSON columns and `Storage.with_db` for all access.\n5. Keep responses deterministic. Do not add randomness or time-dependent\n   behavior.\n6.
